clue.text: Medication on top of operation — hard basis for doing exercises?

parts.note: a tablet is a pill, a dose of medication
OP is the usual short form of operation

explanation.surface: A patient on pills after surgery is told to do exercises on something firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so the medication word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A table surface is a firm flat place on which pupils write out their schoolwork, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I stick to straight sex, other-wise WI's going crazy!

indicators.note: crazy suggests disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
something that is going is leaving, so those letters drop out of the word they sit in

parts.note: the hyphen is just surface; read the word whole
the letters W, I and S, removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: A prim member of the Women's Institute protests that the group is going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the Women's Institute, a British village women's club; here it is just letters to strike from OTHERWISE, leaving OTHERE to rearrange into HETERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A heterosexual person, informally called a hetero, sticks to straight sex, so the phrase describes the speaker.

clue.text: Briefly, doctor and MO seem perplexed, identifying embryonic cells

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so the letters are thrown into a muddled new order

parts.note: DR is the short form of doctor, as 'briefly' says
taken as written
taken as written
joins the pieces of fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor and a medical officer look baffled while examining tissue from an embryo.
explanation.definitionFit: The mesoderm is the middle germ layer of an early embryo, the sheet of tissue from which muscle and bone develop.

clue.text: Almost transfix adult antelope

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: to transfix is to pierce through with a spike
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A hunter nearly spears a fully grown antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful African antelope known for its long leaps, an example of the general class.

clue.text: Unsuitable for children — like this puzzle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: carrying the old adults-only film certificate
second meaning: this grid is crammed with the letter X, so it is rated by its X content

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is the letter X, which appears in nearly every answer; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: X was the British film certificate for adult-only viewing, and this grid is marked throughout by that same letter.

clue.text: Feature of 5 across films has king turning up — an old one

definitions.note: 'one' stands for the king just mentioned, so this means an ancient king

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: 5 across is X-RATED, and adult-rated films feature this
REX is Latin for king, used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: Adult films feature a monarch flipping upside down, as an old one did.
explanation.walkthrough: SEX followed by REX gives SEXREX, which read upwards is XERXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes was a Persian ruler of the fifth century BC, so he is an ancient monarch of the type the clue mentions.

clue.text: Most of 11 note crude sig-nature, American style

indicators.note: most of means everything bar a little, so the last letter of the referenced entry is lost

parts.note: the answer to 11 across
ME is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale, often spelt mi
someone who cannot write signs with a cross

explanation.surface: A message is signed with a rough mark in a transatlantic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tex-Mex is the blended Texan and Mexican cooking and culture found in the southwestern United States.

clue.text: Primitive carving showing cross — old, of unknown origin

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
O is the standard abbreviation for old
short for anonymous, the attribution for an unnamed author

explanation.surface: An ancient carving of a cross, maker unknown, is put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A xoanon is a crude wooden cult statue from early Greek religion, often said to have fallen from heaven.

clue.text: Going under £25, squeeze out previous long-distance mail service

parts.note: pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to express juice or milk is to squeeze it out

explanation.surface: Spending under twenty-five pounds, someone wrings out an old courier deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the squeezing word goes under the money; 'previous' belongs to the definition, since this mail run is long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pony Express was a relay of horseback riders carrying letters across the American West in 1860 and 1861.

clue.text: Cross-examine second of defendants seen in certain bars

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them hard

indicators.note: second of tells us to keep only the letter in position two of the following word

parts.note: its second letter

explanation.surface: A barrister questions the accused, who are then seen behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of metal rods across a window or opening, a particular set of parallel bars.

clue.text: Resin has doubled work with a new US chopper

parts.note: OP, short for opus, a work, written twice
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
AX is the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: A gum resin is used twice in a job involving an American helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but here it is a tool that chops.
explanation.definitionFit: Opopanax is a fragrant gum resin obtained from certain plants and used in perfumery.

clue.text: Races to embrace old flame, offering biblical quotation?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the TT races are the motorcycle Tourist Trophy on the Isle of Man
a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone races off to hug a former lover while quoting scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is a noun naming a famous motorcycle event.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher's text is the passage of scripture a sermon is based on; the question mark admits this is one example.

clue.text: Neat re-packaging of toy range giving vital back-up in major operation

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one

indicators.note: repackaging puts the same contents into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Tidy repackaging of a toy line proves crucial to a big business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like an adjective for the repackaging, but it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: In open-heart surgery a machine oxygenates the patient's blood, taking over from the lungs as essential life support.

clue.text: Close in rough area

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to come near to something
second meaning: as an adjective, not exact, as in a rough estimate of an area

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense (stress on the last syllable) and the adjective sense (stress on the middle) are spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means come near to or nearly equal; as an adjective it means roughly correct but not precise.

clue.text: Lies drunk in place for boxing wine

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy fighter lies sprawled in the boxing ring with a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the aromatic white wine made from it, notably in Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: Unwilling to return to my local office, I emigrated

definitions.text: Unwilling to return to my local office, I emigrated

parts.words: Unwilling to return to my local office, I emigrated
parts.note: surface reading: someone who left the country rather than go back to their usual workplace
setter's reading: a return is a form declaring income, sent to the local revenue office

explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' and 'office' suggest going back to work; read as revenue jargon they are the annual form and the revenue authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves abroad to avoid paying their home country's levies on income is the person described.

clue.text: Annie Lewis

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Scottish singer of Eurythmics
second meaning: the British heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one person's name, but each word is a first or last name completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of singer Annie Lennox is also the forename of boxer Lennox Lewis, world heavyweight champion in the 1990s.

clue.text: Array various pieces of art in combination

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A display brings together assorted artworks in a mixed show.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular grid of numbers or items set out in rows and columns, as in mathematics.

clue.text: A figure to bewitch — one hard to fault!

parts.note: to hex is to put a spell on

indicators.note: a geological fault breaks and shifts the rock, so these letters are dislocated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A spellbinding character is so perfect that nobody can find anything wrong with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to fault' reads as praise, but 'hard' is part of the fodder and 'fault' does the jumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexahedron is a solid shape with six flat faces, such as a cube, so it is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Amateur cricket team — everyone bowling over underarm?

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for amateur
a cricket side has eleven players, written XI

indicators.note: bowling something over knocks it upside down, which in a down clue flips the word end to end

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A village cricket side all bowl underarm, as amateurs might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underarm' looks like a cricket bowling style, but it is the definition, the place under the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The axilla is the anatomical name for the armpit, the hollow beneath where the limb joins the shoulder.

clue.text: Exceptional naval strategist gets a grip on opponents

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the admiral who won at Trafalgar
second meaning: a wrestling hold behind the neck

explanation.walkthrough: A nelson is a wrestling hold in which an arm is passed under the opponent's and the hand pressed on the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was Britain's greatest admiral, and the wrestler's nelson is a hold that pins a rival's head.

clue.text: Verbal expression of today's motif

explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet each letter has a spoken code word, and the theme letter of this grid has this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators spell out the letter X with this code word, so it is the spoken form of the theme letter.

clue.text: Against returning to market in exotic island location

parts.note: anti means opposed to

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the next words are read from right to left

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to going back to the shops lives on a faraway tropical isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antilles are the chain of Caribbean islands, Greater and Lesser, a far-flung tropical archipelago.

clue.text: Put in such a lap as to be among the big money winners?

parts.words: Put in such a lap as to be among the big money winners?

setter's reading: the idiom about living in great wealth and comfort, being in the lap of something

clue.text: Digital means of manipulating vote — European vote

voters mark their choice with a cross
